name: Aarti Pharmalabs Ltd
tagline: Xanthine-derivatives leader with a real CDMO scale-up (40 molecules, +40-50% FY27 guide), but FY26 was a genuine down year and the pivot is capex- and working-capital-heavy with negative FCF and rising debt
business_overview: Demerged from Aarti Industries in Oct 2022, Aarti Pharmalabs is a leading Xanthine-derivatives (caffeine, theobromine) manufacturer now pivoting toward higher-value CDMO/CMO (contract development & manufacturing) work. Commercial molecule count nearly doubled from 21 (FY24) to 40 (3Q FY26). New Atali facility (Phase-1, 450 KL) inaugurated Sep 2025 with 8-10x expansion potential per a trusted community post; Atali Block 2 brownfield (Rs 149 Cr, ~405 KL) approved for CDMO in Q1 FY27.
fundamentals_table: FY26 ROE ~8.6%, ROCE ~11% (3yr avg ~12% / ~17%) - dragged by working-capital intensity and a weak FY26
FY25 Rs 2,115 Cr -> FY26 Rs 1,819 Cr (-14%, forex + labour codes + xanthine pricing); Q1 FY27 rebound +38.7% YoY, PAT +65%
Borrowings Rs 413 Cr (FY25) -> Rs 754 Cr (FY26, +83%); FCF -Rs 112 Cr FY25, -Rs 186 Cr FY26; Crisil AA- Stable
fundamentals_narrative: FY26 was a genuine down year - revenue fell 14% to ~Rs 1,819 Cr and PAT fell ~36% to ~Rs 175 Cr, hit by a ~Rs 33 Cr net forex derivative loss, new labour codes and Chinese pricing pressure on the legacy xanthine base. Q1 FY27 rebounded sharply (revenue +38.7% YoY to Rs 535.8 Cr, PAT +65% to Rs 76.1 Cr, EBITDA margin back to 24.75%) on record xanthine and record CDMO quarters. The CDMO/CMO segment grew 32% in FY26, was ~29% of Q4 revenue, and management guides +40-50% growth in FY27 toward ~USD 100 mn. But the pivot is capital-hungry: ~Rs 400 Cr/yr capex (FY26 and FY27), borrowings up 83% to Rs 754 Cr, negative free cash flow two years running, working-capital-heavy (inventory 190-280 days). Group guidance is a modest 15-18% revenue/EBITDA CAGR over 3-4 years - a compounder profile, not a 10x-in-2-3-years one. Crisil upgraded the bank facility to AA- Stable (Jul 2025). New MD Rashesh Gogri appointed Q1 FY27 (family continuity).
sentiment_summary: Read 50 of 106 available posts (of 122 total) spanning Nov 2024 to Apr 2026. Sentiment stayed constructively bullish throughout, centered on the CDMO pivot: Q4 FY25 concall notes and an Aug 2025 trusted-user post both framed CDMO as the primary forward growth driver, with the Atali facility flagged as having 8-10x future expansion headroom. A brief Jul 2025 wobble occurred when family-trust (Tulip/Orchid, non-operating promoter entities) stake sales were flagged as a "smart money taking chips off the table" concern, but the community largely resolved this as portfolio-reallocation by financial trusts rather than operating-promoter concern, especially once open-market promoter buying was reported in Dec 2025. Most recent substantive post (Apr 2026) covered two regulatory items: a minor Mar 2026 chemical leak at Unit VI Tarapur (22 workers hospitalized for observation, most discharged same-day, no fatalities) and a single-observation FDA Form 483 at Unit IV Tarapur described by the company as "procedural" (unconfirmed until FDA publishes the actual observation text).
community_signal: Prdnt_investor (trusted, 19 loves) explicitly framed CDMO as "the growth driver going forward" and called the Atali site "future proof with 8-10x potential expansion." Naman_Gupta1 (trusted, 20 loves) posted detailed Q4 FY25 concall notes on the CDMO/repeat-order relationship structure. sumit680 (trusted) noted promoters buying ahead of an expected strong H2 on CDMO tailwinds. This is a cluster of trusted-user engagement leaning bullish on the CDMO growth thesis specifically, though none used explicit "core holding"/"X% of portfolio" conviction language.

Family-trust (non-operating promoter) entities reduced holdings through 2025, partly offset by operating-promoter open-market buying reported Dec 2025. verdict_headline: A credible CDMO scale-up with real trusted-user conviction on the thesis, but FY26 was a down year, the pivot burns cash, and management's own 15-18% CAGR guidance is a compounder profile - not a 10x-in-2-3-years one
verdict_reasoning: The molecule-count doubling (21 -> 40) and the +40-50% FY27 CDMO guide are concrete, but the deep read establishes FY26 was materially weak (rev -14%, PAT -36%) and the business runs negative FCF with borrowings up 83% - the growth is being funded by debt

Q1 FY27's strong rebound (+39% rev, +65% PAT, ~25% margin) shows the FY26 weakness was partly transient (forex, pricing), which supports Medium conviction, but the capital intensity and working-capital drag cap it below Medium-High
Management guides 15-18% group revenue/EBITDA CAGR over 3-4 years; at a ~Rs 7,800 Cr market cap that is a compounder, not a 10x - thesis_fit moves to neither

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~36x trailing on a depressed FY26 EPS (~Rs 19); a FY27 recovery to ~Rs 30-35 EPS (Q1 FY27 annualises ~Rs 33) puts the forward P/E at ~26x. To justify 36x trailing at a ~22-24x compounder exit the market needs ~25-30% EPS CAGR FY26-28 - above management's 15-18% group guide but bridgeable off the low FY26 base plus the CDMO 40-50% FY27 guide
